question_en:
I am preparing a cell nucleus segmentation exercise for a new colleague and want to select fields of view suitable for high-density scenarios from the public dataset to which the microscopic image on the screen in the figure belongs. Please first identify this dataset, then answer the following questions:

1. After reviewing all original fluorescence microscopy images in the dataset, which images contain at least 150 nuclei with complete contours that can be individually distinguished from one another? Please list all filenames. Targets that are truncated by the image edge, adhered to other nuclei such that they cannot be distinguished individually, or appear only as blurred light spots are not counted. For each selected image, please describe the sample preparation method, magnification at the time of capture, imaging modality, equipment used, and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) level based on the source record.

Answer format: Use a table to list item by item the filename, sample preparation method, magnification, imaging modality, equipment, and SNR level for all selected images; there is no need to provide a separate list of filenames.

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · P2-8-3-D01

## Step 01 · Deconstruct the problem statement and record judgment units

**Action:** Read the current problem, and separately record image identification, full-set boundaries, visual criteria, and subsequent attribute queries.

**Evidence Observation:**

I am preparing a cell nucleus segmentation exercise for a new colleague and want to select fields of view suitable for high-density scenarios from the public dataset to which the microscopic image on the screen in the figure belongs. Please first identify this dataset, then answer the following questions:

1. After reviewing all original fluorescence microscopy images in the dataset, which images contain at least 150 nuclei with complete contours that can be individually distinguished from one another? Please list all filenames. Targets that are truncated by the image edge, adhered to other nuclei such that they cannot be distinguished individually, or appear only as blurred light spots are not counted. For each selected image, please describe the sample preparation method, magnification at the time of capture, imaging modality, equipment used, and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) level as recorded in the source.

Answer format: Use a table to list item by item the filename, sample preparation method, magnification, imaging modality, equipment, and SNR level for all selected images; there is no need to provide a separate list of filenames.

**Evidence Links:**

Current problem statement, input attachments, and the member table established in the previous step; this step introduces no new web pages.

**Result of this step:** First trace the input, then filter members one by one according to the full set limited by the problem, and finally query the hit objects.

## Step 02 · Locate the public segmentation dataset from the microscopic image

**Action:** Example query: fluorescence nuclei segmentation dataset normal cells neuroblastoma annotated; compare public galleries with the nuclear morphology arrangement on the screen.

**Evidence Observation:**

The input matches the recorded source of normal_0.tif. The number of nuclei in each field of view cannot be determined directly from screenshot brightness. BioImage Archive S-BIAD634 provides access to the original images under the dataset title An annotated fluorescence image dataset for training nuclear segmentation methods.

**Evidence Links:**

https://uk1s3.embassy.ebi.ac.uk/bia-integrator-data/pages/S-BIAD634.html
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7419523/
https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/fire/S-BIAD/634/S-BIAD634/Files/dataset/rawimages/normal_0.tif

**Result of this step:** Determine the dataset accession and enter the original image-level list.

## Step 03 · Define the full set of original fluorescence images

**Action:** Filter TIFF files under dataset/rawimages/ in the BIA file list and cross-check item by item with the official file_list_raw_images.tsv.

**Evidence Observation:**

The page overview shows 388 images and 468 files, including groundtruth, singlecell_groundtruth, JPEG, PNG, and SVG, etc. The problem asks only about 79 raw TIFFs; masks and thumbnails are not counted separately. Counting by four file groups yields 10 + 18 + 41 + 10 = 79.

**Evidence Links:**

https://uk1s3.embassy.ebi.ac.uk/bia-integrator-data/pages/S-BIAD634.html
https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/fire/S-BIAD/634/S-BIAD634/Files/file_list_raw_images.tsv

**Result of this step:** 79 original image filenames serve as the unique member keys.

## Step 04 · Establish original image download and attribute mapping

**Action:** Read the complete FTP address and TSV Files field for each raw image, connect by basename, and check for duplicate names or missing rows.

**Evidence Observation:**

The saved BIA HTML contains 79 raw TIFF addresses, corresponding one-to-one with the 79-row member table; the official TSV provides Preparation, Magnification, Modality, Device, and S/N Class. Retain all attributes first, but inclusion is still determined by the count of complete distinguishable nuclei; high S/N or low magnification cannot substitute for visual screening.

**Evidence Links:**

https://uk1s3.embassy.ebi.ac.uk/bia-integrator-data/pages/S-BIAD634.html
https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/fire/S-BIAD/634/S-BIAD634/Files/file_list_raw_images.tsv

**Result of this step:** Obtain the full set that can be opened image by image and the subsequent attribute table.

## Step 05 · Clarify nucleus instance inclusion rules

**Action:** Check by partitioning the full field of view whether targets are complete and individually distinguishable, prioritizing magnification for boundaries and dense regions.

**Evidence Observation:**

Targets truncated by the edge are not counted; those adhered but still individually distinguishable can be counted, while indistinguishable clumps and blurred light spots are not counted. Official mask IDs can suggest potential nucleus locations, but not all non-edge annotations can be automatically treated as nuclei meeting the criteria.

**Evidence Links:**

https://uk1s3.embassy.ebi.ac.uk/bia-integrator-data/pages/S-BIAD634.html
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7419523/

**Result of this step:** Adopt a threshold of at least 150 effectively visible nuclei.

## Step 06 · Distinguish lower-bound evidence from total count assertions

**Action:** For dense images, cross-check saved per-nucleus coordinates and original image crop audit records, then judge whether the count has exceeded 150.

**Evidence Observation:**

The numbers for the nine positive cases are conservative lower bounds of confirmed visible nuclei, not the precise total count for the full image; unselected targets do not automatically become negative cases. Subsequent per-member records follow existing audits; ordinary NO cases retain only the existing judgment of fewer than 150, without fabricating precise counts or new independent manual reviews.

**Evidence Links:**

https://uk1s3.embassy.ebi.ac.uk/bia-integrator-data/pages/S-BIAD634.html

**Result of this step:** Reconstruct complete member results based on traceable existing judgments.
